title: Roll a ball at a 3 cm step. Does it get up? 0.7 m/s: no, 0.9 m/s: yes. The limit is 0.81 m/s
description:
Roll a ball at a step. Does it get up? Two panels on one clock, side view: the same level floor and the same 3 cm step with a sharp edge, the top level and continuing to the right. A solid ball of radius R = 11 cm (22 cm across, I = 0.4 m R^2, the mass cancels) rolls without slipping at v0 toward the step, spinning at omega0 = v0 / R: top panel 0.7 m/s, bottom panel 0.9 m/s; g = 9.807 m/s^2. The ball's surface at the height of the edge is 7.55 cm ahead of its centre and every lower part is nearer, so the first contact is the edge itself, the centre 43.34 degrees from the vertical over it. The ball grips the edge and never slips there (the grip it needs is printed below). Through the catch the angular momentum about the edge is conserved, so the spin drops to omega1 = omega0 (1 - h / ((1 + k) R)) = 0.8052 omega0 with k = 0.4: the catch keeps 0.8052 of the spin and loses 0.1948, about one fifth. Then the ball pivots about the fixed edge as a rigid body, (1 + k) R phi'' = g sin(phi), a pendulum stood on its head: if (1/2)(1 + k)(omega1 R)^2 reaches g h it goes over the top and rolls on along the step at sqrt((omega1 R)^2 - 2 g h / (1 + k)) with no further loss; if not, it rises (1 + k)(omega1 R)^2 / (2 g), swings back down, the floor kills the downward speed (a plastic landing conserving angular momentum about the floor contact) and it rolls back. Threshold v* = sqrt(2 g h / (1 + k)) / (1 - h / ((1 + k) R)) = 0.8052 m/s. RK4 at dt = 1e-05 s with compensated summation, the events by bisection inside the step, checked against the energy, the closed forms and a half-step rerun. Shown at 1/10 speed on a 10 s cycle, 4 rolls in 40 s. Deterministic, no seed.

Measured:
- geometry: the edge 7.5498 cm ahead of the centre at the touch, phi0 = 43.3418 degrees; the catch keeps 0.8052 of the spin and 0.6483 of the energy; its impulse ratio (tangential over normal) is 0.1135 for any v0, as is the grip the floor landing needs
- threshold v* = 0.8052 m/s; edge-force limit: the edge force is zero at the first touch at 1.1000 m/s, and above it the model ends (a real ball bounces off the edge)
- 0.7 m/s: omega0 = 6.3636 rad/s, omega1 = 5.1240 rad/s, 0.1052 m/s under the threshold; the energy 0.2224 J/kg is under g h = 0.2942 J/kg, so it falls back: highest at 0.1722 s after the touch, the centre 2.2676 cm up (closed form 2.2676 cm, diff -1.0e-15 cm), 0.73 cm short; back on the floor at 0.3443 s moving back at 0.4099 m/s and down at 0.3869 m/s; rolls back at 0.4538 m/s (closed form, diff +0.0e+00) spinning at 4.1258 rad/s; the edge force at least 0.4328 weights and the grip needed at most 0.4531, both at the touch; energy within 2.2e-16 J/kg over 34431 steps
- 0.9 m/s: omega0 = 8.1818 rad/s, omega1 = 6.5880 rad/s, 0.0948 m/s over the threshold; over the edge at 0.1845 s, rolling on at 0.3238 m/s (closed form 0.3238 m/s, diff +0.0e+00) spinning at 2.9437 rad/s; the edge force at least 0.2405 weights and the grip needed at most 0.8155, both at the touch; energy within 2.2e-16 J/kg over 18446 steps
- half-step rerun (dt = 5e-06 s): 0.7 m/s highest at 0.1721521 s, back at 0.3443042 s, rise 2.2675657 cm, rolls back at 0.4538371 m/s; 0.9 m/s over at 0.1844561 s at 0.3238122 m/s; each +0.0e+00 against the full step
- 1.0 m/s: over at 0.1424 s, rolling on at 0.4775 m/s, but the edge force at the touch is only 0.1263 weights and the grip needed 1.553; 0.8 m/s: rises 2.9617 cm, back at 0.7287 s, rolls back at 0.5187 m/s, grip 0.572; 1.1 m/s: the edge force at the touch is 0.0001 weights, the model's limit (over at 0.1194 s at 0.6035 m/s)
- a hollow ball (thin shell, k = 0.6667) of the same size: threshold 0.7104 m/s (it keeps 0.8364 of the spin), edge-force limit 1.0591 m/s
- a 5 cm step for this ball: threshold 1.2393 m/s, but the edge force is negative at the touch above 1.1359 m/s, so no speed takes it: the ball bounces off before it can climb
- a bike-wheel ring (R = 33 cm, k = 1) at a 10 cm kerb: threshold 1.1671 m/s, edge-force limit 1.7701 m/s, keeping 0.8485 of the spin
- 37 checks against the brief, 0 failed

Why: the edge stops the bottom of the ball, so the ball has to pivot over it, carried by the spin and forward motion it keeps through the catch. The catch is a collision: angular momentum about the edge is conserved, but 0.1948 of the spin is lost at once, for any speed. What is left must lift the centre 3 cm. At 0.7 m/s it lifts 2.27 cm, 0.73 cm short, and the ball swings back down and rolls away; at 0.9 m/s it has 0.0948 m/s to spare and rolls on at 0.32 m/s. The limit, 0.81 m/s, is a closed form in the step height, the radius and the inertia factor k: a hollow ball keeps more spin and needs only 0.71 m/s; above 1.10 m/s the first touch would need the edge to pull the ball down, so a 5 cm step cannot be climbed this way at any speed by this ball.
